target_customer: Households in urban Mexico paying in advance for home internet via 7, 15 or 30 day recharges
problem: Residential internet in Mexico required contracts and credit. Siglo sells prepaid fixed wireless access with no contract and rooftop antennas.
business_model: Prepaid recurring home broadband (fixed wireless ISP) with recharge periods

founders.name: Joel Phillips
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page; Forbes Mexico via search says the brothers created Pig.gi.

founders.name: Isaac Phillips
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. CB Insights lists only Isaac as founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Deploying and running fixed wireless networks in dense cities and a prepaid billing system is standard telecom engineering with real operational difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Installed antennas and local network density help, but incumbent ISPs and other fixed wireless providers could serve the same households.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents kept 12 month contract packages per a later guide; no source shows them copying prepaid fixed wireless.

market_need_then: The YC page frames the need as faster, easier to pay internet in urban Latin American communities. Soma Capital job listing (undated) cites 1,700 connected homes and $26,000 monthly recurring revenue.

branding.domain_note: Uses siglo.com, which fits an exact .com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain Spanish consumer language: 'Internet rapido para todos y para todo'

brand_strength.rationale: Short Spanish word meaning century that is shared with many Mexican businesses; a 2018 blog post suggests Siglo began as a product on the Pig.gi user base, but no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Siglo remains an active ISP with about 20 people. Its model of prepaid fixed wireless matches a market with credit and contract barriers, but the only funding figure found is an unverified aggregator seed. Evidence of scale is limited to an undated job listing and a regulatory filing mention in 2024, so success or stall is not determinable from public data.
notes: CB Insights reports a $2.2M seed on 2021-09-10 and total about $2.33M; VCBacked gives August 2021 with amount undisclosed and Seedtable gives 2021-09-01 with no amount. Sources conflict and rely on aggregators only, so no round is recorded. Investors listed by VCBacked: YC, Gaingels, Canary, Goodwater, Acequia. Founding year ranges from 2018 (Soma listing) to 2021 (CB Insights); YC says 2020. A Medium post that likely names incumbents returned 403 and was not read, and no competitor source dated near 2021 was found, so the list is empty. Recheck: siglo.com was opened and names no founders, competitors or funding; no non-aggregator source was found, so nothing was added. Completeness pass: the seed of 2.2M on 2021-09-10 is recorded from CB Insights alone (total about 2.33M over five rounds per CB Insights; other rounds not itemized). Descubre.vc cites a seed of about 4.1M, so amounts conflict and the round rests on a single database. No press source found.
